plan.title: Liver 3-group DE: any-difference LRT + pairwise contrasts
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq from human liver with three unpaired groups (control, treated_a, treated_b; n=4 each), raw Salmon gene-level counts, single batch, no known covariates. The research question has two parts: (1) which genes differ across all three groups at all — answered by a DESeq2 likelihood ratio test comparing the full model (~condition) to the reduced model (~1), which is the correct 'any-difference' ANOVA-like test for a 3+ level factor; (2) which genes each treatment changes vs control — answered by two named pairwise Wald contrasts (treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control) with control set as the explicit reference level. Log2 fold changes for each pairwise contrast are shrunk with ashr (required because a contrast between two non-reference levels is not a single model coefficient, so apeglm does not apply). BH-FDR is computed within each contrast at alpha=0.05 with DESeq2 independent filtering. Downstream, per-contrast fgsea preranked GSEA (ranked on the Wald statistic) is run against MSigDB Hallmark and Reactome gene sets available in the reference store, to characterize the coordinated pathway-level signal beyond single genes. A final report step consolidates the LRT any-difference gene set, the two pairwise DE tables, fit diagnostics, and enrichment results with full reproducibility metadata. This follows the DESeq2 LRT+pairwise-Wald procedure recommended for 3-group unpaired designs with 4 replicates/group and no batch structure.

Benjamini-Hochberg FDR within each contrast, alpha=0.05, independent filtering on
